The problem

  • 1.Constant context-switching

    Agents constantly context-switch between case/incident details, knowledge sources, and tools while crafting responses fragmenting their focus and slowing resolution.

  • 2.Manual tasks, inconsistent quality

    Core tasks like drafting, summarizing, and knowledge search remain manual, producing inconsistent quality across agents.

  • 3.Rigid AI assistance

    Existing AI assistance was too rigid agents couldn’t refine or adapt outputs to their specific case, so they frequently abandoned AI suggestions and reverted to manual effort.

  • 4.AI outside the workflow

    The AI experience lived outside the agent’s natural workflow, creating friction instead of reducing it.

1 / 13

Research and discovery

Workflow Observation

  • Mapped case management across CSM, ITSM, SPM, and HR; pinpointed context-switching and manual effort peaks

Pain Points

  • Starting from scratch, mid-case knowledge search, tool-switching, low trust in AI outputs

Stakeholder Input

  • Collaborated with product, engineering, and domain leads on technical constraints and priorities

Competitive Audit

  • Studied how AI-native products deliver inline assistance and contextual interactions

Key understanding

“Agents don’t need more features, they need AI they can trust that understands their current task and delivers contextual support right where they work.”

Design strategy and framework

  1. Carrier shows the package on hold at the regional hub.

    Draft delay update
    Find hub hold policy
    Summarize this case

    1.Context-first, not feature-first

    Every AI action should be grounded in what the agent is currently working on, not a generic menu of capabilities.

  2. AI draft
    ShorterFriendlierFormal

    2.Edit in place, stay in flow

    AI outputs should be editable in place. Agents should be able to adjust tone, length, and content without abandoning their current task.

  3. CSM
    ITSM
    HR

    3.One framework, many domains

    Design reusable patterns (cards, actions, handoffs) that scale across CSM, ITSM, and HR etc without custom rebuilds.

  4. AI is working · 4 steps
    1. Read the case
    2. Check carrier status
    3. Draft the reply
    4. Update the record

    4.From assistant to collaborator

    Move Otto context menu from single-action responses toward agentic flows where AI can chain multiple steps autonomously.

Persona

  • Agent

    Documenting quality resolutions takes too long.

    Pain points

    • Tab-switching for context
    • Manual notes and summaries
    • Generic AI drafts

  • KB Author

    Articles need time, research, and rewording.

    Pain points

    • Scattered source data
    • Slow rewording
    • Inconsistent structure

  • Creator

    Repetitive writing lowers content quality.

    Pain points

    • Rewriting the same content
    • Quality drops at volume
    • No reusable templates

  • Requester

    Slow filing leads to incomplete submissions.

    Pain points

    • Unclear what to include
    • Long, complex forms
    • Back-and-forth for info

Overview

Issue:

Customer unable to access Outlook email when connected to corporate VPN.

Key action taken:
  • Verified VPN connection is active and authenticated successfully in the network management console.
  • Checked Outlook connectivity logs; identified DNS resolution failure for the mail server while routed through VPN tunnel.
  • Updated VPN split-tunnel configuration to route mail traffic correctly; confirmed Outlook access restored.
